title: Chapter 83
content:
The torrential downpour that had battered the city for the past two hours finally tapered off around midnight.

A sleek executive sedan slipped quietly into the subterranean garage of an ultra-luxury residential high-rise in central Seoul. Tonight’s target was Kim Dong-myung—a black-market broker running high-end sex-trafficking rings for political elites. Fortunately, Kang Il-hyun owned a penthouse in this exact complex, allowing the team to clear building security without raising an eyebrow.

Jakyeong hadn't bothered asking why Il-hyun held real estate here. The senior housekeeper had once casually mentioned that the man’s private property portfolio was virtually impossible to count; this tower was simply another dot on the map.

"Just how obscenely wealthy is this guy?"

"Who knows. Far beyond anything we could imagine."

On paper, Haewon Group operated as a legitimate corporate titan, but beneath the surface, it remained deeply entrenched in illicit trades. Operating with razor-thin precision along the fringes of the law, their legal team routinely cleared executive investigations without charges—greased, no doubt, by colossal kickbacks delivered to the right desks.

Leaving Wang Han on standby in the vehicle, Jakyeong and Wang Ryun hauled their gear bags—loaded with suppressed sidearms, tactical ropes, and combat blades—toward the private elevators.

A swipe of the biometric keycard opened the doors. They rode up to the fifteenth floor, slipping into the concrete fire escape to ascend the remaining flights to the roof.

The heavy steel access door at the top was deadbolted. Ryun pulled an electronic bypass rig from his kit, sending a high-voltage pulse through the locking mechanism before prying the latch open. They slipped onto the gravel-topped roof, methodically sweeping the perimeter.

Finding an optimal drop point, Ryun looped a high-tensile climbing rope around a heavy industrial HVAC unit, securing the line with dual locking carabiners. He hauled back on the cord multiple times to test the load. Satisfied, the two men stepped to the ledge, lighting cigarettes side by side.

Beneath them, the rain-washed city sprawled out in a brilliant, breathtaking sea of neon and glass.

Exhaling a plume of smoke into the cool air, Ryun let out a low chuckle. "Hell of a skyline."

"Yeah."

"What do you think? Didn't you say you grew up somewhere around this district?"

Jakyeong surveyed the sea of high-rises. It wasn't this exact neighborhood—a few kilometers off, though the precise coordinates had faded from memory. Back then, Seoul had never looked like this. To a starving, terrified ten-year-old child fighting to survive each night, the city had been nothing short of a living hell.

"Once this contract wraps," Ryun mused, "maybe I'll set up our newlywed home right here in Seoul. With the cash we've banked, buying a whole commercial building outright would be light work."

Jakyeong shook his head without looking over. "Pass. The second my twelve months are up, I'm out of this country."

Ryun grinned around his cigarette. "You honestly think President Kang is just going to open the cage and let you fly away?"

"I couldn't care less what that lunatic wants."

"Tough talk. From what I’ve seen, the man looks ready to chase you straight past an island and down into the depths of hell."

Jakyeong didn't buy it. He had crossed paths with men like Kang Il-hyun his entire life. When an intriguing new toy caught their eye, they stopped at nothing to seize it; the moment it was firmly in their grip, they discarded it without a second thought. Right now, Il-hyun was only obsessed because the prize remained just out of reach. Once fully possessed, the illusion would shatter.

A quiet click broke through their earpieces, followed by Wang Han’s hushed voice:

[Target has arrived. Taking the private elevator up.]

"Is he alone?"

[Yeah. Heavily intoxicated. Stumbling on his feet.]

Perfect. This should be quick and clean.

The residential tower stood twenty-four stories tall—a sheer drop capable of inducing vertigo with a single glance down the facade. The mark was holed up on the nineteenth floor.

As Jakyeong stretched his shoulders to loosen his muscles, Ryun’s phone vibrated violently against his tactical vest.

Jakyeong’s brow knit into a sharp scowl. Who brings an active personal cell on a live hit?

"My bad," Ryun whispered with a sheepish grin, taking three steps back. Hearing the hushed, sickeningly sweet tone, it was clearly his girlfriend.

Jakyeong attached the suppressor to his automatic pistol, glaring at the back of his brother’s skull, half-tempted to put a warning round through the man's heel.

Ending the call, Ryun sauntered back with an easy, lingering grin.

"I'm telling Han-ge," Jakyeong muttered. "Taking personal calls during an active breach."

"Don't be so uptight, little brother. Remember whose hands are holding your lifeline tonight."

Jakyeong raised the suppressed muzzle, leveling it squarely at Ryun’s forehead. "Looks to me like your life is in my hands."

"Watch the attitude. It only takes one of my fingers to pin you down."

Ryun cheekily wiggled his middle finger in Jakyeong's face. Jakyeong cursed under his breath, clipping the climbing harness securely to the tactical carabiner.

He checked the luminous dial on his tactical watch, planted his boot on the concrete coping, and leaned his weight back over the void. The harness took the load as he kicked off the wall, descending into the dark.

Ryun tracked the line, keeping the cord clear of sharp corners.

Jakyeong rappelled down the sheer concrete face, floor by floor. At past two in the morning, nearly every window was pitch-black.

Reaching the nineteenth-floor terrace, a sudden drizzle began pelting the glass, slicking the masonry.

Fuck. Jakyeong glanced up through the rain, spotting Ryun’s dark silhouette leaning over the ledge above.

Swinging his weight laterally, Jakyeong planted a boot onto the wet balcony railing. He peered through the sheer curtains—the interior was completely dark, suggesting the drunk target had already passed out.

Yet beneath the patter of rain, a sudden, cold prickle crawled up his spine.

He reached behind his tactical belt, his fingers brushing empty air. Damn it. In his haste, he had left his thermal night-vision monocle on the rooftop.

Nothing is going right tonight.

He tapped his throat mic, keeping his voice to a bare whisper:

"Ryun-ge. Lower the thermal goggles on the secondary line."

[Always so careless,] Ryun's voice crackled back. [Hold on.]

Moments later, the optic unit slid down the guide line. Jakyeong caught it, securing the lens over his right eye.

Looking into Kim Dong-myung’s dark living room, his blood ran cold.

Through the greenish-gray thermal spectrum, half a dozen heat signatures stood scattered across the room. Adjusting the focus, heavily armed operatives in full tactical loadouts were positioned in dynamic ambush formations, weapons trained squarely on the balcony glass—waiting for him to breach.

A setup.

Jakyeong whispered urgently into the comms:

"It's a trap. Abort."

[What did you say?!] Han’s alarmed voice crackled in his ear.

Ryun’s channel remained dead silent.

Suddenly, the taut climbing rope jerked violently.

Jakyeong snapped his head up. Through the driving rain, a figure was leaning far over the rooftop railing.

"Ryun-ge?"

The rope snapped taut, then violently loosened. Bracing both boots against the brickwork to steady his balance, Jakyeong wiped the rain from his eyes, his heart hammering against his ribs.

"Ryun-ge, respond!"

Dead silence.

[Wei, talk to me! What’s happening up there?!] Han barked over the line.

Through the downpour, Jakyeong realized the silhouette staring down from the rooftop was far too broad to be Wang Ryun.

The harness line gave way, plunging beneath his weight.

Reacting on pure instinct, Jakyeong kicked off the concrete with explosive force, throwing his entire body into a desperate sideways dive toward the balcony.

Snap.

The severed rope whipped past into the void.

Before he could find his footing, the sliding glass doors shattered in a deafening eruption of gunfire.

Automatic rounds chewed through the terrace wall.

Four armed operators advanced through the glass. The lead shooter raised a clenched fist, signaling a temporary ceasefire.

From the master bedroom hallway, Kim Dong-myung poked his head out, clutching a silk bathrobe around his soft frame. His face was flushed red with alcohol, his eyes glazed and manic.

"Did you get him?! Is the bastard dead?!"

A wall switch flipped, flooding the trashed living room with bright light.

Sprawled across the shattered glass of the balcony lay Jakyeong, motionless.

Kim Dong-myung looked around at the splintered furniture, cursing violently. "Fuck! Do you have any idea how much this interior cost?!"

The mercenary lead gestured for the target to step back, nodding at a subordinate to confirm the kill.

The operative took two cautious steps forward—

In a blinding flash, the 'corpse' on the floor flipped onto its back.

Jakyeong’s suppressed pistol coughed once, putting a round cleanly through the advancing operator's forehead.

Without pausing, Jakyeong swept his aim low, emptying the magazine into the exposed shins and knees of the remaining shooters.

One collapsed with a shattered kneecap, screaming as Kim Dong-myung shrieked in terror, scrambling back toward the bedroom.

Jakyeong threw himself into a lateral roll, tucking behind the structural concrete divider on the terrace.

A hail of return fire chipped away at the masonry, peppering his hair with plaster dust.

Panting heavily, Jakyeong slapped a fresh magazine home, quickly checking his body. A stray 9mm round had grazed his left bicep, opening a warm, bleeding trench along the muscle.

He hissed through his teeth, clamping down on the pain.

As the tactical standoff stretched across the dividing wall, Han’s frantic voice cut through the comms:

[Wei! Are you hit?!]

Jakyeong ground his molars together. "We walked into an ambush. Get to the roof now. Ryun-ge is compromised."

The rain intensified outside, yet the apartment fell into a suffocating, deadly quiet.

Jakyeong grabbed a heavy ceramic planter from the corner, hurling it across the open doorway. The decoy drew an immediate burst of suppressive fire, shattering the pot into dust.

Timing the lull, an operative leaned out to clear the angle. Jakyeong anticipated the peek, putting a single round through the man's eye before he could acquire the target.

Down below, the sustained gunfire had begun waking the complex; lights were flickering on across neighboring towers.

The police will be swarming the perimeter in minutes. I have to wipe this room and extract immediately.

Jakyeong scanned the balcony. Ten feet to his right hung the adjacent terrace—the private balcony attached to the master suite Kim Dong-myung had fled into.

Looking down, the nineteen-story drop was a sheer, dizzying abyss. With the handrails slick from rain, a single missed grip meant plunging to the asphalt. Yet pinned down by armed professionals in a narrow kill-box, holding out was suicide.

He had no other play.

Holstering his weapon, Jakyeong rubbed his wet palms vigorously against his tactical trousers.

Come on.

He mounted the outer railing and launched himself across the open air.

His boots fell short, but his gloved fingers clamped onto the cold metal of the opposite balcony.

Hauling his body weight over the ledge, he glanced through the open terrace doors.

Kim Dong-myung was pressed flat against the bedroom door, trembling like a leaf as he tried to listen to the gunfire in the hall.

Right on schedule.

Jakyeong stepped through the open slider, pressing the cold steel of his suppressor firmly against the base of Dong-myung’s skull.

The broker spun around, his eyes bulging in sheer terror as his knees completely buckled. The arrogant, swaggering predator who had casually offered to traffic children a year ago had dissolved into a sobbing, pathetic mess.

Jakyeong used the trembling man as a human shield, twisting the bedroom handle and stepping into the hallway.

Rounding the corner into the living room, the remaining two mercenaries spun around, instantly raising their rifles.

Both wore black tactical balaclavas, their weapon handling polished and disciplined.

Jakyeong dug the barrel deeper into Dong-myung’s neck. "Drop your weapons if you don't want your employer's skull ventilated."

Neither man moved an inch.

Seeing the cold indifference in their eyes, Kim Dong-myung screamed at the top of his lungs: "Drop the fucking guns! Do you want to see me die, you useless bastards?!"

The operators didn't even blink.

A dark realization struck Jakyeong: These aren't bodyguards hired by Kim Dong-myung.

Whoever had bankrolled this hit team, the broker was entirely expendable.

Without missing a beat, Jakyeong shoved Dong-myung forward as a meat shield, advancing behind him while squeezing the trigger: Pfft, pfft.

The lead mercenary caught a double-tap to the chest and head, dropping instantly. The second dove behind an interior pillar just as a spray of return fire tore through Kim Dong-myung’s torso and thighs.

Dong-myung shrieked, thrashing in agony. Jakyeong dragged the bleeding weight forward, using the dying body to close the gap toward the pillar.

The silence returned, punctuated only by the loud, rhythmic ticking of a designer wall clock.

Beneath the quiet, the faint metallic scrape of a magazine release clicked from behind the concrete.

Jakyeong shoved Dong-myung aside, rounding the corner with his weapon raised.

The mercenary, who had just seated a fresh mag, froze with the barrel leveled inches from his brow.

Jakyeong kept his aim steady, reaching out with his left hand to rip the balaclava away.

His expression twisted in surprise.

A foreigner. Barely out of his teens, with terror-stricken eyes.

"P-Please..." the boy whispered in broken English, trembling violently. "Don't kill me... please..."

Jakyeong stared into the young face with cold, detached eyes.

Jakyeong had picked up his first gun at eighteen. He had taken his first human life at nineteen. Staring at this terrified kid felt like looking into a cracked mirror of his own past—but in this line of work, sympathy was a fatal luxury.

He squeezed the trigger.

The suppressed round punched through the forehead, spraying dark crimson across Jakyeong’s cheek.

Wiping the blood from his brow, Jakyeong turned back toward the hallway.

One loose end remained.

Kim Dong-myung was dragging his shredded legs across the polished floorboards, desperately trying to reach the front door.

Jakyeong walked over, planting a heavy boot onto the man's shattered femur.

A bloodcurdling scream tore from Dong-myung’s throat.

Jakyeong rolled him onto his back, staring down with glacial detachment.

"You knew we were coming tonight, didn't you?"

Dong-myung’s face was a grotesque, purplish mask of agony. "I... I don't know what you're talking about!"

"Talk," Jakyeong said, his voice dropping into a lethal register. "Who leaked our approach?"

Tears mixing with sweat, Dong-myung let out a broken, delirious cackle. "Fuck you... you think I'd... tell you? If I talk, they'll skin me alive anyway—"

Crack.

Jakyeong put a round straight through the center of his forehead without blinking.

As the body went limp, Wang Han’s voice crackled frantically through the earpiece:

[Wei! Are you alive?!]

Jakyeong wiped the blood from his slide, stepping over the corpses toward the exit. "Yeah. I'm fine. The apartment is cleared."

[Thank God...] Han exhaled, though his voice carried a faint, unsteady tremor.

A knot of dread tightened in Jakyeong’s chest. "Where is Ryun-ge?"

Silence stretched over the channel.

Jakyeong gritted his teeth, his voice rising in panic: "Han-ge! Where is Ryun?!"

When Han finally spoke, his voice cracked with unshed tears:

[He's bleeding out... He’s completely unresponsive, Wei. We have to get him to a hospital right now.]
